clue.text: Pub drink curtailed amidst tense fracas

indicators.note: a tail cut off means the word loses its final letter
amidst places the shortened drink in the middle of the pub word

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A drinker's pint is cut short when a tense brawl breaks out in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the fracas, but it is the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance, and an incident is a euphemism for exactly that kind of brawl or occurrence.

clue.text: Hit writer reportedly ready for holiday

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: the writer of a clue refers to themself as I
a traveller whose suitcases are filled says they are packed

explanation.surface: A popular author announces they are ready to go on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, the writer declaring 'I'm packed' gives the answer; the setter's I is the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the force of one object striking another, so it is a hit or collision.

clue.text: Jumper Dad left during 7-0 win finally found in clubhouse

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the abbreviation for left goes inside the number
finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a cricket is a jumping insect
pa is a familiar word for father
seven in Roman numerals
L is the abbreviation for left
zero looks like the letter O
the closing letter of win

explanation.surface: A sweater, left by Dad after a 7-0 victory, was recovered from the sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, which fits a sports pavilion, but it is the insect. 'During' inserts L between the first two strokes of VII and the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket pavilion is the building at a cricket ground where players change and members gather, so it is a clubhouse.

clue.text: Process order containing climbing pants

indicators.note: containing says the two words hold the letters within them
in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of process and the start of order

explanation.surface: An instruction to process a purchase order for trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British slang for rubbish, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang 'pants' means worthless rubbish, and dross is worthless waste matter.

clue.text: Abruptly ended trip before finishing, out of petrol required

indicators.note: abruptly suggests being cut off suddenly, so the word loses its final letter
to trip is to stumble, so the shortened word falls into a new order
out of means without, so one letter is taken from the petrol word

blocks.note: taken as written
petrol is fuel
the finishing letter of before

explanation.surface: A journey ends suddenly before completion because the car has run out of petrol needed to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDE(D) is rearranged; then the last letter of 'before' is removed from FUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is a slightly old-fashioned adjective meaning necessary, so it means required.

clue.text: Queen has retired vicar a-flutter

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the following letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Qu. is an abbreviation for queen
Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
a means one, which is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The Queen has a retired clergyman who is all of a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'a-flutter' disguises that 'a' is a separate piece of wordplay; only 'flutter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver is to tremble or shake rapidly, just as something fluttering moves with quick light vibrations.

clue.text: The same eternal problem probing universal dimension

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so the letters must be rearranged
probing means poking inside, so the rearranged letters go between the other two

blocks.note: U is the film certificate meaning universal
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for dimension

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that the same old puzzle keeps investigating the dimensions of the universe.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unaltered has not changed, so it remains the same.

clue.text: Run out of lacquer with fear old manuscript inside's to fade

indicators.note: run out of means without a run, so the cricket letter for a run is removed
inside puts the old manuscript within the word for fear

blocks.note: varnish is a lacquer
fright is sudden fear
O is the abbreviation for old
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: An ancient manuscript, stripped of its lacquer and handled fearfully, begins to fade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is the cricket abbreviation R, which is what comes out of the lacquer word; the old manuscript goes into fear after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish from sight is to disappear from view, which is what fading away completely means.

clue.text: Easter's fitting holiday at last to relax

indicators.note: fitting suggests the letters are fitted together in a new arrangement
at last keeps only the closing letter of holiday

blocks.note: taken as written
the closing letter of holiday

explanation.surface: An Easter break is the ideal holiday for finally unwinding.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest easy is an idiom meaning to stop worrying and feel at ease, so to relax.

clue.text: One inspiring person organised run for detainee

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so these letters are put into a new order
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the one is drawn inside the other letters

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An inspirational figure has organised a run, perhaps a charity race, on behalf of someone held in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: PERSON and R are rearranged, and I goes inside them after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner is someone held in detention, which is exactly what a detainee is.

clue.text: First to join uniform-wearing workers' excursions

indicators.note: the workers are wearing the letter as clothes, so it sits inside their word

blocks.note: the opening letter of join
worker ants are the classic crossword workers
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: New recruits must join the uniformed staff on their outings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to join' means the first letter of join, J; U then goes inside ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunts are short pleasure trips, so they are excursions in the everyday sense.

clue.text: Legal document set down brief

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to set down words is to write them

explanation.surface: A lawyer drafts a document and lays out a legal brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like a lawyer's brief, which fits the legal surface, but it is the shortening signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order, a type of legal document.

clue.text: Tearooms hosting king put out fine buns

indicators.note: hosting means taking in a guest, so the king's letter is brought into the tearooms word
put out means evicted, so the letter for fine is thrown out to make room for the newcomer

blocks.note: cafes are tearooms
K is the chess abbreviation for king
F stands for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: The tearooms that served a king put out some fine buns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out fine' tells you to remove F from CAFES, and K takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Buns are small sweet baked goods, so they are a kind of cakes.

clue.text: Example of a setter's puzzle

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse or muddle, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Here is a sample of what a crossword compiler can do.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the fodder to the indicator: 'of a setter' is puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is a small early sample of what is to come, so it serves as an example.

clue.text: Wait perhaps taking on students when convenient

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
L for learner, doubled for more than one student

explanation.surface: A queue of students might have to wait until whenever it suits.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British cars, so students become LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever you choose, which is when convenient.

clue.text: Brought back sad reveries about November

indicators.note: sad suggests something in a sorry state, so the letters are disordered
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the month

blocks.note: taken as written
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Melancholy daydreams about November bring back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought back' is the definition, a past-participle phrase like 'in reverse' after a verb such as 'driven'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moved in reverse travels backwards, so it is brought back the way it came.

clue.text: Harrassed staff gathering right information for taxes

indicators.note: harassed staff are flustered and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order
gathering means collecting something in, so the jumbled staff surround the next letters

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
I is the symbol for information, as on tourist signs

explanation.surface: Overworked civil servants collect the correct data needed to set import taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue spells 'Harrassed' with a double R; that is the setter's spelling and does not affect the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties levied on imports or exports, so they are taxes.

clue.text: Hesitate when mediocre journalist to pen article on Britain

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a pen, so the journalist's word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: a hack is a second-rate writer
an is the indefinite article
GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: A writer pauses before agreeing to write a piece about Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like the writer's tool, but here it means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang back is an idiom for holding back from acting through reluctance, which is to hesitate.

clue.text: Exchange of letters with artist in Manga style

indicators.note: style suggests the word is restyled, its letters given a fresh look
in places the artist inside the rearranged comic word

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: An illustrator corresponds by letter in the style of Japanese comics.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: the answer names the very device the wordplay uses.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram rearranges the letters of a word, so it is literally an exchange of letters' positions.

clue.text: Naughty girl gets cross after a short time

indicators.note: after says the cross comes second, following the short time

blocks.note: min is short for a minute
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A mischievous girl gets angry after a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to mean angry, but it is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a cheeky, impudent girl, the stock term for a naughty young woman.

clue.text: Graduate finally forfeited post for shoddy work

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word it follows, keeping just its closing letter

blocks.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
the closing letter of forfeited
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A graduate finally lost the position because the work was poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad job is an idiom for a poorly done piece of work, which is shoddy work.

clue.text: Panicky bather initially encouraged to fill lungs

indicators.note: someone panicky is all over the place, so the letters are scrambled
initially keeps just the opening letter of encouraged

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of encouraged

explanation.surface: A panicking swimmer is urged to take a deep breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe in is to draw air into the lungs, so to breathe is to fill them.

clue.text: Pay heed to top grade race finish

blocks.note: A is the highest grade
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Take note of the top-rated finish in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to something is to give it your attention, which is to pay heed to it.

clue.text: Complaint from good Republican regularly riles Vice President

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
R is the abbreviation for Republican
the second and fourth letters of riles
JD Vance is the US Vice President

explanation.surface: A grumble from a decent Republican who keeps getting irritated by the Vice President.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance is a cause for complaint, or the complaint itself, against perceived unfair treatment.

clue.text: Advantage with Alcaraz beginning second part of match

indicators.note: beginning keeps only the opening letter of the player's name

blocks.note: the opening letter of Alcaraz
S is the abbreviation for second
a tennis match is divided into sets

explanation.surface: In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz has the advantage as the second set begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advantage' sounds like tennis scoring, which fits Alcaraz the Spanish champion, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource that gives you an edge, so it is an advantage.

clue.text: Last letter's in gold on blue

indicators.note: in puts the last letter inside the chemical word for gold

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
re means on, as in regarding

explanation.surface: Heraldry: the final letter is painted in gold on a blue background.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the bright blue of a clear sky, and also blue in heraldry.

clue.text: Housing for workers is good in areas beside railway

indicators.note: in places the word for good inside the abbreviation for areas

blocks.note: A for area, doubled for the plural
pi, short for pious, means good in crossword usage
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Accommodation for railway workers is good in areas near the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The workers are bees: an apiary houses beehives.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where beehives are kept, and worker bees are the 'workers' it houses.

clue.text: Take pains with horse involved in poor result

indicators.note: poor suggests the word is in bad shape, its letters spoiled into a new order
involved in means wrapped up inside, so the horse sits within the jumbled letters

blocks.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jockey takes great care with a horse that came in with a disappointing finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle is to make great effort against difficulty, which is what taking pains means.

clue.text: More sympathetic when family brought back wine!

indicators.note: brought back means returned the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: kin are family
red is a wine

explanation.surface: Relatives are more understanding when they've come home with a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinder means showing more kindness, which is being more sympathetic.

clue.text: Smashed act of daring crossing river delta

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the river's word straddles the act of daring

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a feat is a bold deed
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A daring stunt ended in a crash while crossing the river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River delta' reads as a single geographical place, but it splits into the river and the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed in the sense of thoroughly beaten, as a team is smashed or defeated by an opponent.
